segments.text: You choose the wound over the balm, and the ruin over the rose.
Very well. The candle burns low, but it does not die.
Yet the empty chairs will not be forgotten. They shall wait for you at every table, in every house, until you learn to sit among them.
Farewell, the play will find another stage.

events.custom_event_name: [THE SICKLY YELLOW SKY DISSOLVES INTO DARKNESS AS THE HEAVY PULL OF THE ABYSS SLOWLY FADES AWAY]

segments.text: William's mind returns from Carcosa. William looks around; his surroundings begin returning to normal, the mask is shattered, and the old wounds still remain.

events.name: Special
events.custom_event_name: [THE ROTTING RITUAL ROOM OF BLACKWOOD MANOR IS QUIET ONCE MORE, LIT ONLY BY THE FAINT MOONLIGHT FILTERING THROUGH THE BROKEN WINDOWS]

segments.text: He steps out of the room and looks over the place, picturing his family, the trauma, and the wounds from the past. For the first time, he no longer runs from the ghosts of what happened here. He carries the weight of it all as he walks toward the front doors. Even though the actor refused his stage, there will always be another story waiting to unravel.

events.custom_event_name: [THE CAMERA SLOWLY PULLS BACK, DRIFTING OUT OF THE SHADOWY HALLWAY, PAST THE DECAYING WALLS OF THE MANOR, AND INTO AN ENDLESS, PITCH-BLACK VOID WHERE A TALL YELLOW FIGURE STANDS]

segments.text: The scene zooms out, revealing that the narrator is actually The King in Yellow himself, reading calmly from the script he holds in his hands.

events.name: Special
events.custom_event_name: [THE KING SLOWLY CLOSES THE PAGES AND TURNS HIS FACELESS, HOODED GAZE DIRECTLY TOWARD THE SCREEN]

segments.text: I have told thee of the house, of the hearth gone cold, and of the sorrow that sleeps in its walls.
But a story is never only what is told.
There is another twist behind the curtain, and soon the players shall step into the light.
You will stay in there until you learn that this family's name and business are worth far more than your life.
Charles’s voice sounded muffled through the thick door, followed by footsteps walking away up the stairs.

events.name: PlaySoundEffect
events.path: [<MUFFLED CRIES FROM BEHIND THE BASEMENT DOOR>]

segments.text: Inside the cold darkness of the basement, young Will curled up in the corner against the wall, hugging his knees and staring at his fingertips, blackened with ink and shaking uncontrollably.
Meanwhile, on the second floor, Margaret had just tucked Diana into her warm bed and kissed her forehead before turning off the lamp.

As soon as the bedroom door closed, Diana turned around to face the rain-streaked window. She reached into the pocket of her nightgown and pulled out her father's small wooden ruler—the exact tool she had used earlier to nudge the ink bottle from behind the chair so her fingertips wouldn't get a single drop of black stain on them. She had then slipped it neatly under her mattress before closing her eyes peacefully.

It was sweet, quiet Diana who whispered of Nathaniel’s midnight walks, leading William’s eyes to his secret with the maid. It was her small hand that stole the handkerchief and laid it beside the poisoned hound in the cellar, lighting the fuse of the boy's wrath.

And on that final night, while the household drank the sleeping draught and sank into darkness, Diana poured hers silently into the linen at her lap. She lay upon the cold stone among the fallen, eyes open in the dark, watching Charles set the stage and waiting patiently for William, the final actor, to return.
The stage may be empty now… yet my play is far from over. Even as thou watch this curtain fall, she’s still out there… setting another stage, waiting for the next play.
